observations: body L1-L2, L17: in the head the dash after «d)» measures 9.5 pt, those of «1–8» and «12–15» 5.4 and 5.3 pt; the dashes after «I.» and «II.» measure 10.3 and 10.8 pt, that of «1–2» 5.4 pt.
body L6, L10, L16, L20, L24, L26, L28, L30, L33: the dashes of «al–Battānī», «al–Battanī», «al–Ma’mūn», «’l–qarnayn» and «al–Bīrūnī» are long dashes (4.7 to 5.6 pt).
body L15, L31: the hyphens of «al-Battānī» measure 2.6 and 2.9 pt.

body L5-L8: the heads stand over braces. Al-Battānī's motions are those of his table of single Roman years (Part II, p. 103), which gives the motions of 20 years to the thirds. Ptolemy's daily mean motions in longitude (Almagest IX, 3) give in 7305 days 244° 38′ 1″ 37‴ 47⁗, 247° 12′ 33″ 49‴ 53⁗ and 228° 15′ 22″ 17‴ 21⁗, printed with the thirds 38, 49 and 17. The differences are right. The rules under Ptolemy's numbers of Saturn and Mars print broken.

body L9-L11: 37 times the differences of L8 gives the sums of Saturn and Jupiter, 2° 54′ 19″ 54‴ and 3° 5′ 22″ 49‴; for Mars 37 × 0° 6′ 48″ 32‴ = 4° 11′ 55″ 44‴, against the printed «45‴». The 740 years stand for the 743 from 137 to 880.
body L12-L13: a brace joins «Tabula Probata» and «Ḥabash (2)»; the numbers stand between the two lines.

body L17-L19: with al-Battānī's precession of 1° in 66 years over the 743 years from 137 to 880 (11° 15′), Ptolemy's apogee of Jupiter, 11° of Virgo (Almagest XI, 1), comes to 172° 15′, 7° 47′ more than al-Battānī's 164° 28′ (L31).
body L20: the beginning of the year 1191, 1 September 879, is that of note 3 on p. 114.

body L25, L28: 1 muḥarram 420 is 19 January 1029 in the astronomers' reckoning from Thursday 15 July 622 (20 January in the civil reckoning); from 880 to 1029 there are 149 years, and 149 years at 1° in 66 years make 2° 15′.

body L26-L32: al-Bīrūnī's longitudes are rightly counted from the beginning of Aries in L30, and the differences of L32 are right. Al-Battānī's apogees are those of p. 114 (L11-L12 there), Mars with the printed 126° 18′; the addenda (Part I, p. LXXI) read 58′ for these minutes, which would make the difference of Mars 1° 32′. The rules under the numbers of Jupiter, Venus and Mercury print broken.
body L28: the a of «al–Battanī» has no macron; kept as printed.

body L33: the minutes are written in Arabic letters: مج 43 and مح 48 differ by the dot of the jīm, كط 29 and لط 39 by kāf and lām. The second of Venus is printed «نط» (59), with the tooth and the dot of a nūn, where the sense requires لط (39); kept as printed. With 43′ and 29′ the differences of Saturn and Venus become 2° 15′.
body L5, L12, L16: specks to the right of «Mars», after the last «20‴» and after «esse.» are not transcribed.
notes_right L1: the dash before «Elementa» measures 8.8 pt and the hyphen of «41,r.-49,v.» 3.6 pt.

body L20-L22: the apogees «pro anno 137» that Nallino compares on p. 241 are Ptolemy's for the epoch of Nabonassar, 747 B.C., 8° 50′ less than those for Ptolemy's own time; see the observations on p. 241.
